lines.japanese:
雑誌を閉じてため息をついた時、樋口章二が何を
言うか、忍にはだいたい予想がついていた。
lines.english: When Shouji Higuchi closed the magazine with a sigh, Shinobu already had a fair idea what he was going to say.

lines.japanese:
言葉を反復してみる。
　いまいち実感が湧かない。
lines.english: He repeated the words to himself. They didn't quite ring true.

lines.japanese: 「そいつを語るには、言葉は不便すぎるぜ……」
lines.english: “Words are too clumsy to explain a thing like that...”

lines.japanese:
わけがわからない。
　ただ直感で、こう思った。
lines.english: It made no sense. But instinct told him one thing.

hyperlinks.preview: A condition in which one imagines an ideal shared by some unspecified collection of men, then mistak

japaneseHyperlinks.preview: A condition in which one imagines an ideal shared by some unspecified collection of men, then mistak

lines.japanese: 「バイクと言っても、原付なんかじゃない」
lines.english: “And when I say motorcycle, I don't mean some moped.”

lines.japanese: 章二はなぜか遠い目をした。
lines.english: For some reason, Shouji gazed into the distance.

lines.japanese: 「ナナハンだったら、僕も持ってる」
章二は椅子の上でずれた。
lines.english: Shouji slipped sideways in his chair.
“I’ve gotten quite a bit of mileage out of it.”

lines.japanese: 「おまえ……いつの間に……型はなんだ？」

lines.english: “Let's see... I think it was the FT.”

lines.japanese:
「……オレの知識にはないな。
　まさか……ビンテージものだとでも言うのか！？」
lines.english: “...Never heard of it. Don't tell me... it's some vintage machine!?”

lines.japanese: 少し昂奮している章二。

いつも無理して作っているクールさが抜けてみっ
ともない感じだ。
lines.english: The cool facade he was always straining to maintain had fallen away. It wasn't a pretty sight.

hyperlinks.preview: Made by T○. Sound Nanahan 75○FT. 3-band radio. Manufactured… early 1970s. Capable of FM transmission

japaneseHyperlinks.preview: Made by T○. Sound Nanahan 75○FT. 3-band radio. Manufactured… early 1970s. Capable of FM transmission

lines.japanese:
「ＧＴもあったけど、
　そっちは捨ててしまったみたいだ」
lines.english: “There was a GT too, but I think that one got thrown away.”

lines.japanese:
「……なにが乗ってるだ……紛らわしい言い方しや
　がって……この腹黒野郎が」
lines.english: “…‘Quite a bit of mileage,’ my ass… Talk about misleading, you devious bastard.”
“Wonder if I can still pick anything up on it.”

lines.japanese: いろいろといじってると、音が鳴り出した。
lines.english: He fiddled with it until sound crackled out.

lines.japanese: 章二がそれを手に取る。

「アナログラジオじゃねぇか。
　よくこんなもん取ってあったな」
lines.english: “An analog radio? I can't believe you held on to this thing.”
“Now I'm shocked for a whole different reason.”

lines.japanese:
「とにかく、オレ様が欲しいのはラジオなんかじゃ
　ない。バイクだ」
lines.english: “Anyway, what I want isn't some radio. I want a motorcycle.”

lines.japanese: 「……なんとかなる。現物さえありゃいいんだ」
lines.english: “...I'll work something out. All that matters is getting the bike.”

lines.japanese: 「値段はいくらくらいなんだろ」
忍は雑誌をぱらぱらとめくった。閉じた。
lines.english: Shinobu flipped through the magazine, then snapped it shut.
“There's no way you can afford one of these.”
“I can if I work hard enough.”

lines.japanese:
「マシーンがいる……男には自分の世界があるんだ
　……そのためにマシーンが……マシーン号が……」
lines.english: “I need a machine… Every man has a world all his own… and for that he needs a machine… the Machine…”

lines.japanese: 「ま、見てろ。じきに手に入れてやるさ」
lines.english: “Just watch. I'll have one before long.”

lines.japanese: 「ま、いいけどね。章二の金だし」
「目標ができるとオレは凄い男だ。見てろよ」
lines.english: “Give me a goal and I'm unstoppable. You'll see.”

lines.japanese:
こうして樋口章二のマシーン獲得の長く険しい旅
がはじまるのである。
lines.english: Thus began Shouji Higuchi’s long and arduous quest to acquire a machine.

lines.japanese: 顔を出すなりそう宣言した。
lines.english: He announced it the moment he appeared.

lines.japanese:
ソファの上であずさと対戦型のカードゲームを遊
んでいた忍に、脇に抱えていた封筒を投げる。
lines.english: Shinobu sat on the sofa playing a competitive card game with Azusa. Shouji flung him the envelope tucked under his arm.

lines.japanese: くるくると回転しながら、封筒が忍のもとに飛ぶ。
lines.english: The envelope spun through the air toward Shinobu.

lines.japanese: あずさ（運動神経良）が叩き落とした。
無様に這いずり、封筒の砂を払う章二だ。
lines.english: Shouji scrambled after it on all fours and brushed the sand off the envelope.

lines.japanese: 「今いいとこなんだから邪魔すんでね」
lines.english: “We're at the good part, so don't bug us.”

lines.japanese: じろりとソファ上の戦場を眺める。
lines.english: He glared at the battlefield spread across the sofa.

lines.japanese: 自分の椅子を引き寄せ、背もたれを前に座る。
lines.english: He dragged over his chair and sat astride it, facing the backrest.

lines.japanese: 「おまえの負けっぷりを見届けてやる」
lines.english: “I'll stick around and watch you lose.”

lines.japanese: ゲームはまだはじまったばかりだった。
lines.english: The game had only just begun.

lines.japanese:
無数のカードから選んだ６０枚（カード一種類に
つき四枚まで）を一つのデッキをそれぞれ持ち寄り、
対戦するのである。
lines.english: Each player assembled a sixty-card deck from countless possibilities (with no more than four copies of any one card) and brought it to battle.

lines.japanese:
最初の手札は７枚で、交互に一枚ずつ引いて戦う。
　いろいろなカードを駆使して、相手のライフを０
にしたら勝ち。
lines.english: They began with seven cards in hand, then took turns drawing one at a time. Using every card at their disposal, they tried to reduce the opponent's life total to zero. Whoever did so won.

lines.japanese:
あずさは自分の初期の手札を見て、うんうんと頷
いた。
lines.english: Azusa studied her opening hand and nodded sagely to herself.

lines.japanese:
敵のモンスターは火力で除去しながら、パワフル
なクリーチャーで一方的に攻撃するデッキだ。
lines.english: Her deck burned enemy monsters off the field, leaving her powerful creatures free to attack.

lines.japanese: 素知らぬ顔で、忍はデッキをシャッフルしている。
lines.english: Shinobu shuffled his deck with a look of perfect innocence.

lines.japanese:
「だってね、だってね、なんか最初のターンに０マ
　ナで出てくるクリーチャーがいて、それ生贄に捧
　げて４マナとか使えるカードがあってね」
lines.english: “But, but, listen! On the first turn he played some creature for zero mana, then sacrificed it and played this card that gives him four mana or something!”

lines.japanese:
「なんかいろいろぐるぐるまわってこっちに順番
　まわってくる前にライフなくなっちゃったよ？」
lines.english: “Then all this stuff kept going around and around, and I was out of life before I even got a turn!”

lines.japanese: 「１ターンキルという小さな奇跡が起こったんだ」
lines.english: “A small miracle known as a one-turn kill occurred.”

lines.japanese: 「……おまえもそんなえげつないの使ってやるな」
lines.english: “...You didn't have to use something that nasty on her.”

lines.japanese: 「もう一個の、ゾンビデッキの方でやる？」
lines.english: “Want to try my other deck? The zombie one?”

lines.japanese: あずさはゾンビが嫌いだった。
忍は大きく伸びをした。

lines.english: “So, you said you bought a motorcycle?”

lines.japanese: 渡されたパンフレットを見る。
lines.english: He studied the brochure Shouji handed him.

lines.japanese: 「仕方ないので、５０ＣＣからはじめることにした」
lines.english: “I had no choice, so I'm starting at fifty cc.”

lines.japanese: 「だがこいつは原付だがけっこう高いぞ」
lines.english: “It may be a moped, but it's an expensive one.”

lines.japanese: 「……ローマの休日に出てきたやつに似てるね」
lines.english: “...It looks like the one from Roman Holiday.”

lines.japanese: 「全然ハードじゃないじゃん」

「フォルムの美しさが硬派なんだよ。
　猿はモンキーにでも乗ってろって感じだな」
lines.english: “The beauty of its lines is what makes it macho. Monkeys can stick to riding Monkeys.”
“Delivery's set for the end of the month.”
Azusa had caught him off guard.

lines.japanese: 助けを求めて忍を見る。
lines.english: He looked to Shinobu for help.

lines.japanese:
「……こいつはフットペダルだから、
　ちょっと難しいんだぞ？」
lines.english: “...It's got a foot pedal, so it's harder than it looks, you know?”

lines.japanese: 「バイクこうやって乗ってるの、やってみたい」
lines.english: “I wanna do that thing where you ride like this.”

lines.japanese:
あずさが椅子をバイクに見立てて、ハングを切っ
ている。
lines.english: Azusa straddled the chair as though it were a motorcycle and hung off the seat into a turn.

lines.japanese: 膝が地面をこするほど傾き、すてんと転んでしまう。
lines.english: She leaned until her knee nearly scraped the floor, then toppled over.

lines.japanese:
たいしたもので、危なげもなく手をついた。
　椅子は音を立てて転がった。
lines.english: Impressively, she caught herself without the slightest trouble. The chair went clattering away.
“I'm going to take good care of it!”

lines.japanese: 「なんか違う。今の章二かっこわるい」
lines.english: “Something's off. You looked really lame just now, Shouji.”

lines.japanese:
「じゃあちゃんと乗るから、とりあえずここに納車
　しようよ」
lines.english: “Then I'll be really careful. Just have them deliver it here.”

lines.japanese:
指定先を工場にして、章二は待っていた。
　少年のような忍耐力で、入口に立っていた。
lines.english: Shouji had given the factory as the delivery address and was waiting there. He stood at the entrance with all the patience of a little boy.

lines.japanese: 「ここはわかりにくいから、立ってないとな」
lines.english: “This place is hard to find. Somebody has to stand out here.”

lines.japanese: 「なんだ？　用事ならあとで―――」
lines.english: “What? If you need something, it can wait—”

lines.japanese: あとは静かでおだやかな時間が流れるのみであった。
lines.english: After that, time passed quietly and peacefully.

lines.japanese:
あまりにも遅れているため、忍がそう提案したの
だった。
lines.english: The delivery was so late that Shinobu finally made the suggestion.

lines.japanese:
章二は携帯を取り出す。
　アンテナを見ると、五本とも立っている。
lines.english: Shouji took out his phone. All five signal bars were showing.

lines.japanese: 「配達には時間通りに出たらしい」
lines.english: “Apparently it went out for delivery on time.”

lines.japanese: 「ちっ、使えない店だぜ。醒めるな」
lines.english: “Tch. What a useless shop. Way to kill the mood.”

lines.japanese:
二人は諦めて、工場に入った。
　結局この日、原付が納車されることはなかった。
lines.english: The two of them gave up and went into the factory. In the end, the moped never arrived that day.

lines.japanese:
原付を乗せたトラックごと、どこかに失踪してし
まったのだそうだ。
lines.english: Apparently the entire delivery truck, moped and all, vanished somewhere.

lines.japanese: 返金はされなかったという―――

「最近、朝も夕方も顔を出さない裏切り者の章二だ
　わ」
lines.english: “Look who it is—Shouji the traitor, who never shows his face in the morning or the evening anymore.”
“Don't call me that, Four-eyes... It was beyond my control.”

lines.japanese:
「これ外してどんなことになっても知らないわよ？
　あんた責任とれんの、ああ？」
lines.english: “If I take these off, whatever happens is on you. Got that? You ready to take responsibility, huh?”

lines.japanese:
「とりあえず久しぶりだけど……
　なんかボロボロなのはどうして？」
lines.english: “Anyway, it's been a while... Why do you look like hell?”

lines.japanese: 壁に背をつけて、その場でへたり込む章二だった。
lines.english: Shouji leaned against the wall, slid down it, and crumpled to the floor.

lines.japanese: 衣服は汚れ、髪は乱れ、肌も張りを失っている。
lines.english: His clothes were filthy, his hair disheveled, and his skin drawn.

lines.japanese: 「あんた、ちょっと臭うわよ？　お風呂入ってる？」
lines.english: “You kind of stink. Have you been taking baths?”

lines.japanese:
息も絶え絶えに何か呟く。
　仲間の顔を見て、張りつめていた糸が切れたのか
も知れない。
lines.english: He mumbled something, barely breathing. Perhaps the sight of his friends had finally snapped the thread that had kept him going.

lines.japanese:
「え、なに？　三日もほとんど何も口にしてない？
　捜査であと一歩のところまで追いつめて、食料調
　達せずに山奥に追跡？」
lines.english: “What? You've barely eaten anything in three days? You almost had your target cornered, then chased them into the mountains without stopping for food?”

lines.japanese:
「トラックの荷台に乗り込んで山奥まで？
　徒歩で帰ってきた？」
lines.english: “You climbed into the back of a truck and rode it into the mountains? Then walked all the way back?”

lines.japanese: 「とりあえずなんか食べさせないと。ごめん、笛子」
lines.english: “We need to feed him. Sorry, Fueko.”

lines.japanese:
笛子は少しだけ眉をひそめた。
　すぐに元に戻る。若干の穏やかなものになって。
lines.english: Fueko frowned for just a moment. When her face settled again, it had softened a little.
“...Honestly. I was looking forward to it.”

lines.japanese: 「今度つきあうから、参考書選び」
lines.english: “I'll help you pick out study guides another time.”

lines.japanese: 「いーわよ。別にすぐいるってもんでもないし」
lines.english: “Fine. It's not like I need them right away.”

lines.japanese: 「それよりそこの難民をなんとかしないとね」
lines.english: “Anyway, we'd better do something about our refugee over there.”

lines.japanese:
「ごちそーさま。
　便乗していいもの食べさせてもらいました」
lines.english: “Thanks for the meal. I got to tag along and have something wonderful too.”

lines.japanese:
卓上に並べられた大量の皿。
　三人でたいらげた、忍の手料理だ。
lines.english: A mountain of empty plates covered the table. The three of them had polished off Shinobu's cooking.
“Everything tastes better when we eat together.”

lines.japanese: 「せいぜいしっかり働くんだな」

「うわ、いい香り。ふれーばーふれーばー。
　どこの紅茶？」
lines.english: “Oh, that smells wonderful. Flavor, flavor. What kind of tea is it?”

lines.japanese: 包みを見て、笛子はのけぞった。
lines.english: Fueko recoiled when she saw the package.

lines.japanese: 「あんたの姉上様、あなどれないわね……」
lines.english: “Your illustrious sister is not to be underestimated...”

lines.japanese:
「ここの紅茶、日本にしか輸出してないのよ。
　日本でもなんとかってデパートでしか買えない
　ってことだから」
lines.english: “They only export this tea to Japan. And even here, you can only get it at some department store or other.”

lines.japanese:
「いやー、あの若さで一軒家持つだけのことはある
　ってことね……勉強しよ、私も」
lines.english: “No wonder she owns her own house at her age. I'd better study harder myself.”

lines.japanese: 「同じ店のものと思われるスコーンもあるよ」
lines.english: “Looks like there are scones from the same shop too.”

lines.japanese: 手掴みでわしゃわしゃ食べる二人だ。
lines.english: The two of them shoveled the scones down with their bare hands.

lines.japanese:
争奪戦。
　別腹とはよく言ったもので―――
lines.english: A feeding frenzy. They weren't kidding about having a separate stomach for dessert—

lines.japanese:
スコーンをたいらげて、三人は同時に吐息を落と
した。
lines.english: When they'd demolished the scones, all three of them sighed at once.

lines.japanese: それぞれソファに身を預けて、昼寝の勢いだ。
lines.english: They sprawled across the sofa, ready to nap the afternoon away.

lines.japanese: 「こんな幸せな土曜日、滅多にないわ……」

「これでこの汗くさい男がいなければどんなにいい
　か」
lines.english: “If only this sweaty man weren't here, it would be even better.”

lines.japanese: 「なんでレスホームになってたわけ？」
lines.english: “How did you end up less-home, anyway?”

lines.japanese: 「……って、このあいだ盗難されたアレ？」
lines.english: “...The one that was stolen the other day?”

lines.japanese: 「お金返してもらえなかったっていう？」
「その原付を追っていた、つまり？」
そして章二は語り始めた。

「盗難届けは出したがこんなご時世だ。
　そうそう見つかるものでもないと思ってた」
lines.english: “I reported it stolen, but these are the times we live in. I wasn't expecting it to turn up anytime soon.”

lines.japanese: 「そこでオレは、自力で捜査を開始することにした」
lines.english: “So I decided to launch my own investigation.”

lines.japanese:
「といっても本職の警察じゃないからな。
　毎日歩き回ったわけじゃない」
lines.english: “I'm no real cop or anything. It's not like I spent every day walking the streets.”

lines.japanese: 「ところがある日、偶然オレは見たんだ」
lines.english: “Then one day, by pure chance, I saw it.”

lines.japanese:
「……オレ自らがデザインした代紋が塗装された、
　原付をな―――」
lines.english: “...A moped bearing the crest I designed myself—”

lines.japanese: 「おまえにノーズアートの何がわかる！」
lines.english: “What do you know about nose art!?”

lines.japanese: 「いやそれ、ノーズアートじゃないし……」
「とにかく、間違いなくオレの原チャだったんだ」

「ああ……オレは徒歩だったから、走って追いかけ
　た。ホシはフルフェイスをかぶっていたから、顔
　はわからない。捕まえるしかなかった」
lines.english: “Yeah... I was on foot, so I ran after it. The perp had a full-face helmet on, so I couldn't see their face. I had to catch the rider.”

lines.japanese:
「オレは走った。信号待ちでなんとか距離を詰めた
　りもしたが、結局無理だった」
lines.english: “I ran. I managed to close the distance whenever it stopped at a red light, but in the end it was hopeless.”

lines.japanese:
「原付は国道に合流する道に乗った。
　だからオレは、咄嗟の判断で同じ流れに乗って
　いたトラックの荷台に転がり込んだ」
lines.english: “The moped took a road that merged onto the national highway. So I made a split-second decision and threw myself into the bed of a truck going the same way.”

lines.japanese: 「すでに体力は限界だった。走り続けていたからな」
lines.english: “I was already at the limit of my endurance. I'd been running nonstop.”

lines.japanese: 「乗り込むと同時に、オレは意識を失った」
lines.english: “The moment I climbed aboard, I blacked out.”

lines.japanese:
「目覚めたのは夜、峠のような場所だった。
　オレはそこにうち捨てられていた」
lines.english: “I woke up that night somewhere that looked like a mountain pass. I'd been dumped there.”

lines.japanese:
「無一文で、峠を降りて場所を確認しここまで戻る
　のに……三日かかった……」
lines.english: “I didn't have a cent. I came down from the pass, figured out where I was, and made my way back here... It took three days...”

lines.japanese: 「むしろよく三日で帰れたと」
lines.english: “Honestly, it's impressive that you made it back in only three days.”

lines.japanese:
「怒りがオレを突き動かした。
　だが……悲しいものだ、人とは」
lines.english: “Rage kept me going. But man is a sorry creature...”

lines.japanese:
「腹がくちくなると、嵐のような感情が嘘のように
　消え去ってしまった」
lines.english: “The minute my belly was full, the storm of feeling inside me vanished as if it had all been a lie.”

lines.japanese:
「あんた原付で死にかけたんだけど……
　それって単に安堵、じゃなくて？」
lines.english: “You nearly died over a moped... Isn't that just relief?”
The two men gazed into the distance.
Fueko held her head in her hands.
“So the investigation is back to square one.”

lines.japanese:
忍は重々しい口ぶりで、まるで世界の破滅に抗す
る重要人物であるかのような峻厳な態度でもって、
章二に告げた。
lines.english: With all the grave solemnity and stern bearing of a great man defying the end of the world, Shinobu told Shouji:

lines.japanese:
「命をかけて、何も手にはない。そんなことを許し
　ていいものだろうか？」
lines.english: “You put your life on the line and have nothing to show for it. Can we let that stand?”

lines.japanese: 「樋口章二ともあろうものが―――」

「……このままにはしておけねぇ。オレの金、オレ
　の三日、オレの原付……そいつは絶対に取り戻す
　べきものだからな」
lines.english: “...I can't let this stand. My money, my three days, my moped... I have to take back what's mine, every last bit of it.”

lines.japanese:
野獣のような男の双眼が、ぎらぎらと輝きを取り
戻していくのが笛子にもわかった。
lines.english: Even Fueko could see a beast's savage gleam returning to his eyes.

lines.japanese: 「世界を敵に回そうとも、原チャ返せって感じだな」
lines.english: “The whole world can turn against me—just give me back my damn moped.”

lines.japanese:
「こうしちゃいられねぇ……飯も食ったし、一旦知
　り合いを当たって情報収集だ」
lines.english: “No time to sit around... I’ve eaten. First I’ll hit up some people I know for information.”

lines.japanese: のそのそと大股に、立ち去るのであった。
lines.english: He lumbered away in long strides.
“...Everything about his life is way too entertaining.”

lines.japanese: 「いやぁ、あんたアジテーターの才能あるわねー」
lines.english: “You'd make one hell of a rabble-rouser, you know.”

lines.japanese:
「まさかあんな映画みたいなことしてるとは思わな
　かったから……そこまで行くならと思って」
lines.english: “I had no idea he'd done anything straight out of a movie... Once he'd come that far, I figured he might as well keep going.”

lines.japanese:
「もし返ってこなくても、十年後くらいにはいい思
　い出になるはずだし」
lines.english: “Even if he never gets it back, ten years from now it should make a good memory.”

lines.japanese:
「さて、肉肉しいのがいなくなったところで、
　ベノア茶おかわり」
lines.english: “Now that the big slab of man-meat is gone, another cup of Benoist.”

lines.japanese:
気怠い午後が過ぎていく。
　世界は平和だった。
lines.english: The languid afternoon drifted by. The world was at peace.
